description:
ContactStore::upsert() and upsert_discovered_contact() use SQLite's 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE ...' clause to make the UPDATE a no-op when no column value changed, then check rows_affected to decide whether to advance the state counter. This prevents spurious state advances when peers repeatedly call Peer/deliver with the same sender metadata.

Same pattern appears in set_blocked(), set_presence_fields(), and the outbox enqueue_receipt(). The WHERE clauses use IS NOT comparisons (NULL-safe) rather than != so NULL-to-NULL is correctly treated as 'no change'.

This is correct and subtle. The alternative (always advance state on upsert calls) would cause JMAP clients to poll /changes on every incoming message even when no contact metadata changed, producing empty /changes responses and unnecessary round-trips. Worth defending against suggestions to simplify by removing the WHERE guard and always advancing.
title: DECISION: idempotent upserts only advance state counter on actual change
